propositions: The production in-process verifier (`verify-completion` with isolated verdict-cache namespaces and `source='local'`) achieves 100% per-AC agreement (65/65) on the corpus with 0 rejections on real ACs across 9 runs.

A minimal free-tool harness agent (Copilot CLI, no rebar scaffolding) produces 5 false-FAIL verdicts on real ACs (all concentrated on the epic) despite 0 false-PASS on planted ACs, yielding 94.6% agreement (87/92).

The predeclared GO condition (Arm B rejections strictly < Arm A rejections) fails: 5 vs 0; the hypothesis that unreliability stems from in-process scaffolding rather than task design is not supported on this corpus.
Wall-time comparison favors production verifier at 3× median speed (131 s vs 415.5 s); Arm B cost is free locally but spans full test-suite execution overhead.

Arm B defends epic AC7 (stamp and mapping mutation land in one commit) and AC2 (enrichment data present) as strict-literal failures due to multi-commit implementation; these represent plausible coverage gaps worth follow-up rather than harness fragility.
